correctness.rationale: The actual RESULT.md gives a complete proof for two specific base-three planar IFS digit masks D3={0,e1,e2} and D6={(a,b)>=0:a+b<=2}. Infinite Fourier-product tails are nonzero in the absence of finite mask zeros, since deviations from one are summable. For a primitive 3^s character, cyclotomic divisibility by 1+t^(3^(s-1))+t^(2*3^(s-1)) forces equal coefficient counts in every 3-coset; for s>=2 their modulo-three aggregate counts must be divisible by three. Direct eight-pair residue count rules this out for D6 (counts (3,2,1) permutations or (2,2,2)); D3 has no higher primitive zero. At s=1 both masks vanish iff primitive coordinates are (1,2) or (2,1) mod3. Joint 3-adic valuation therefore gives exactly the stated integer zero set, layer density sum_{v>=0}2/9^(v+1)=1/4 and level-L count (9^L-1)/4. Open-set condition for the six and three disjoint triangle maps gives support dimensions log_3(6) and 1; Fourier characters diagonalize both torus convolutions. Fresh independent exact cyclotomic enumeration across primitive order 3,9,27,81 tested 8,72,648,5832 primitive pairs and found 2,0,0,0 zeros for each mask; level-L totals for L=1..4 were 2,20,182,1640. The computations are corroboration, not an infinite proof.
